english.html: for one may well teach certain speeches, and give tokens and marks: but to impart the knowledge of so many and so many divers persons, never seen or known — that is impossible, otherwise than by Magic or some reprobate art. And so much for the matter of the proof by witnesses. In the second place, a summary inquiry having been made upon the likeness of the accused with the sisters of Martin Guerre, it is reported — and better still by several witnesses heard in the inquiries on the court's own motion — that eggs are not more alike among themselves.

The ancient proverbs of like things have most often been taken from eggs, or from milk, from water, or from honey-bees. Would you not have (says Cicero in some place) the proverb be true, of the likeness of eggs, so great that it is very hard to discern and tell apart the one from the other? And a little after: As eggs, says he, are like to eggs, and honey-bees among themselves <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>. And Sosia in Plautus, seeing Mercury to have taken his form, and to resemble him in everything, said: Milk is not more like to milk than that fellow is to me <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>. Messenio also, speaking to Menaechmus of Sosicles: Water, says he, is not so like to water, nor milk to milk, as Sosicles is to you, and you to him <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>.

notes.citation: Cicero, Academica II (Lucullus), §§ 54–57 (the proverbial likeness of eggs, and of bees)
notes.original: Ciceron au ij. liure des Academiques.
notes.gloss: Lucullus 54: videsne ut in proverbio sit ovorum inter se similitudo?; the argument is that the Stoics cannot tell twin eggs or bees apart, yet claim infallible perception. Section numbers unverified.

notes.citation: Plautus, Amphitryon, line 601 (neque lac lacti magis est simile quam ille ego similest mei; line number unverified)
notes.original: Plaute en la premiere comedie, inſcripte Amphytrion.
notes.gloss: Sosia, having met his double Mercury; "the first comedy" as at annot-003, Amphitruo standing first in the plays.

notes.citation: Plautus, Menaechmi, lines 1089–1090 (neque aqua aquae nec lacte est lactis, crede mi, usquam similius, quam hic tui est, tuque huius autem; line numbers unverified)
notes.original: Plaute en la comedie de Menechmus.
notes.gloss: Messenio the slave, on the two Menaechmi; the twin of Syracuse is Menaechmus Sosicles, Coras's Soſides.

uncertain.text: mais de bailler la congoiſſance de tant,
uncertain.note: sic: the print sets 'congoiſſance' (c-o-n-g-o-i-ſſ-a-n-c-e) where the sense requires 'cognoiſſance'; the g and the o are transposed. Verified at 300%; the double s is a true ſſ (both sorts long), unlike 'impoſsi-' two lines above.

uncertain.text: mais veuës ni cognues: cela eſt impoſsi-
uncertain.note: 'impoſsi-' is long s + round s, not ſſ. Verified at 400% and again on margin-1.jpg where the same word falls at the crop edge; the second sort is plainly the short round s.

uncertain.text: blãce du preuenu, auec les ſeurs de Mar
uncertain.note: the mark over the a of 'blãce' is a tilde, not an acute: it is a broad, slightly wavy horizontal stroke, whereas the acute of 'rapporté' / 'reprouué' in the same size of type is a thin near-vertical wedge (both compared at 500%). Reading is 'ſemblãce' broken 'ſem-' / 'blãce'.

uncertain.text: mouſches à miel. veux-tu pas (dit en quelque lieu Ci-
uncertain.note: sic / turned sort: the first letter of 'mouſches' is an m lying on its side (rotated 90 degrees), which is why the print shows a wide gap after it. Transcribed as an upright m because the turned form cannot be represented; verified at 400%.

uncertain.text: ſemblables, dit. il, les œufs aux œufs, & les mouſches à
uncertain.note: the print really sets 'dit. il,' with a period between the two words (round dot on the baseline, matching the other periods on the page), not a comma. Verified at 450%.

uncertain.text: re auoir prins ſa forme, & le rapporter en tout, di-
uncertain.note: the line-end break sign after 'di' is printed as a small round dot sitting on the baseline, not as the short slanted stroke used for the hyphens of 'Ci-', 'entre-' and 'Mercu-' on the same strip (all four compared at 600-1000%). Transcribed as '-' per the convention that any line-end word-break sign is written '-' (the word is 'diſoit'), but it could equally be read as a period sort set in error: 'di.'

uncertain.text: Soſides: L'eau, dit'il, n'eſt pas ſi ſemblable à l'eau, ni le
uncertain.note: 'dit'il' is printed with an apostrophe, not a hyphen; verified at 600%. Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: enu, quand fut confrontee audit du
uncertain.note: sic: the word is broken 'pre-' (end of the previous line) / 'enu,' here, so the print gives 'pre-enu' where the sense requires 'preuenu'; the u is missing. Both line ends verified at 500%; there is no u and no second hyphen.

uncertain.text: ij. liure des A-
uncertain.note: the numeral is the italic 'ij' (short i plus a j with descender, one dot); at reading size it can look like a single 'y'. Read as 'ij.' (= Cicero, Academica II) at 1000%.

uncertain.text: Menechmus.
uncertain.note: the final stop is a round dot on the baseline with a faint second mark just above and right of it; most likely a period plus ink, but a worn colon cannot be ruled out. Transcribed as a period.

a stray vertical ink stroke (roughly ascender height, no identifiable letterform) stands in the margin beside the first line of the annotation, 'Les prouerbes anciẽs … ont eſté le', well above the first margin note. It is not transcribed; it may be an offset, a bit of furniture or a reader's mark.

uncertain.text: mais de bailler la congoiſſance de tant,
uncertain.note: sic: printed 'congoiſſance' (n before g), not 'cognoiſſance'; ſſ ligature.

uncertain.text: blãce du preuenu, auec les ſeurs de Mar
uncertain.note: the mark over the a of 'blãce' is a short curved stroke (breve-like) rather than a wavy tilde; read as the nasal tilde (= blance/blāce for 'semblance').

uncertain.note: diaeresis printed over the e of 'veuës'; 'impoſsi-' is long s + round s; the stop after 'cognues' read as a colon (two dots), set tight.

uncertain.text: ANNOTAT. XLIII.
